title: Finite relative Tor dimension of a perfect tensor
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme], f:X -> S any scheme morphism, E a perfect object of D(O_X) [def-pc-perfect-complex], and G a bounded complex of O_X-modules whose terms are flat over S [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then E tensor^L G [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] has finite Tor dimension over the inverse-image structure sheaf f^{-1}O_S [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension-over]. No coherence, Noetherian hypothesis, locally finite type or proper-support hypothesis is needed.

source.place: 0DJQ: relative Tor verification; 08CI and 08CG: bounded flat models and locality

proof.text: Choose a global complex K representing E tensor QG using DerivedCategory.Q.objPreimage and its object-preimage isomorphism. Restrict K to the inverse-image base ring and take a K-flat resolution P -> Kbase. These choices occur only in a proposition of existence, not in new data definitions.

Unpack IsPerfect to choose a strictly perfect neighbourhood U_x and representative L_x for each point. Extract term bounds [a_x,b_x] from strict perfectness and [c,d] from boundedness of G. The local bound theorem applied to the fixed K,P,q gives vanishing of sections of every relative tensor homology sheaf on all V contained in U_x outside [a_x+c,b_x+d].

Compactness gives a finite subcover. Insert 0 in the finite lower and upper endpoint sets and take their minimum lo and maximum hi. Then lo <= 0 <= hi, lo <= a_x+c and b_x+d <= hi on every selected chart. These inequalities send a degree outside [lo,hi] outside the selected local interval. At each point choose a chart of the finite cover containing that point.

For each test module F and degree outside [lo,hi], let M be the relative total tensor homology sheaf. Prove IsZero M by showing its identity equals zero. On an arbitrary open W, the opens W intersect U_x cover W; the local bound gives zero sections on every intersection. Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' makes every section on W zero. The resulting global vanishing, K,P,q and the ordered interval witness HasFiniteTorDimensionOver. In the empty-cover case both endpoints are 0 and sheaf separatedness for the empty cover gives the same result.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0DJQ, 08CI, 08CG; local chart calculation isolated, finite subcover and relative homology sheaf gluing proved in Lean

lean.statement:
theorem perfect_tensor_hasFiniteTorDimensionOver
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] (f : X ⟶ S)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : IsPerfect X E)
    (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hGb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (G.X n))
    (hGflat : ∀ n : ℤ, Modules.IsFlatOver (G.X n) f) :
    HasFiniteTorDimensionOver f (E ⊗ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G)
